---
id: ingress-controllers-nginx-ingress-snippet-annotations
name: "NGINX Ingress snippet annotations"
description: "Installs NGINX Ingress with allowSnippetAnnotations=true, creates an Ingress with configuration-snippet annotation injecting add_header X-Test, verifies the header appears."
labels: {customer: any, profile: ingress}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: ingress-nginx/ingress-nginx
      version: "4.10.0"
      release: ingress-nginx
      namespace: ingress-nginx
      repo:
        name: ingress-nginx
        url: "https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx"
      values:
        controller:
          service:
            type: NodePort
          allowSnippetAnnotations: true
          ingressClassResource:
            name: nginx
            enabled: true
            default: false
            controllerValue: "k8s.io/ingress-nginx"
          watchIngressWithoutClass: true
        admissionWebhooks:
          enabled: false
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 3m
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/nginx-snippet-ingress.yaml
      namespace: sample
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    image.repository: "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx"
    image.tag: "1.27-alpine"
    ingress.enabled: "false"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: ingress-nginx
    timeout: 3m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/nginx-snippet-annotations.sh
tags: [nightly]
mechanisms: ['addon:nginx-ingress']
category: networking
integration: nginx-ingress
tier: live

scenario.yaml 2293 B · 80 ln

---
id: ingress-controllers-nginx-ingress-tls-cert-manager
name: "NGINX Ingress TLS with cert-manager"
description: "Installs cert-manager + NGINX Ingress, creates self-signed ClusterIssuer+Certificate, verifies HTTPS routing through nginx with TLS terminated by cert-manager-issued cert chain."
labels: {customer: any, profile: tls}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: jetstack/cert-manager
      version: v1.14.0
      release: cert-manager
      namespace: cert-manager
      repo:
        name: jetstack
        url: "https://charts.jetstack.io"
      values:
        installCRDs: true
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 3m
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/selfsigned-clusterissuer.yaml
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/ingress-tls-certificate.yaml
      namespace: sample
    - kind: helm
      chart: ingress-nginx/ingress-nginx
      version: "4.10.0"
      release: ingress-nginx
      namespace: ingress-nginx
      repo:
        name: ingress-nginx
        url: "https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx"
      values:
        controller:
          service:
            type: NodePort
          allowSnippetAnnotations: true
          ingressClassResource:
            name: nginx
            enabled: true
            default: false
            controllerValue: "k8s.io/ingress-nginx"
          watchIngressWithoutClass: true
        admissionWebhooks:
          enabled: false
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 3m
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/nginx-tls-ingress.yaml
      namespace: sample
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    image.repository: "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx"
    image.tag: "1.27-alpine"
    ingress.enabled: "false"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: cert-manager
    timeout: 3m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: ingress-nginx
    timeout: 3m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/nginx-tls-cert-manager.sh
tags: [nightly]
mechanisms: ['addon:cert-manager', 'addon:nginx-ingress']
category: networking
integration: nginx-ingress
tier: live

scenario.yaml 1763 B · 69 ln

---
id: ingress-controllers-traefik-basic
name: "Traefik basic IngressRoute"
description: "Installs Traefik, creates an IngressRoute for the product Service, and verifies HTTP routing through the Traefik pod IP with Host header matching."
labels: {customer: any, profile: ingress}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: traefik/traefik
      version: v28.3.0
      release: traefik
      namespace: traefik
      repo:
        name: traefik
        url: "https://traefik.github.io/charts"
      values:
        image:
          registry: ghcr.io
          repository: traefik/traefik
        ingressClass:
          enabled: true
          isDefaultClass: false
        ingressRoute:
          dashboard:
            enabled: false
        ports:
          web:
            exposedPort: 80
          websecure:
            exposedPort: 443
        service:
          type: NodePort
        providers:
          kubernetesIngress:
            enabled: true
          kubernetesCRD:
            enabled: true
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 3m
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/traefik-basic-ingressroute.yaml
      namespace: sample
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    image.repository: "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx"
    image.tag: "1.27-alpine"
    ingress.enabled: "false"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: traefik
    timeout: 3m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/traefik-basic.sh
tags: [nightly]
mechanisms: ['addon:traefik']
category: networking
integration: traefik
tier: live

      mountPath: "",
      # -- Volume type for the TLS material. Supported: secret (default), persistentVolumeClaim, projected, csi.
      volumeType: "secret",

      pvcClaimName: "",
      # -- SecretProviderClass name (required when volumeType is csi).
      secretProviderClass: "",
      # -- Whether to run the wait-for-tls initContainer that polls for cert files. Disable for CSI volumes that are populated asynchronously.
      waitForCerts: true},
    # -- Scope component (API server). Creates a separate Deployment + Service on port 8080.
    scope: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, service: {port: 8080}},
    # -- Darkroom component (async processor). Creates a separate Deployment with optional PVC mount.
    darkroom: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, pvc: {enabled: false, claimName: "", mountPath: /data}},
    # -- Ingress resource for skywatcher Service.

scenario.yaml 1767 B · 69 ln

---
id: ingress-controllers-traefik-ingressroute-crd
name: "Traefik IngressRoute CRD"
description: "Installs Traefik, uses IngressRoute CRD exclusively for routing (no classic Ingress), and verifies HTTP traffic reaches the backend."
labels: {customer: any, profile: ingress}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: traefik/traefik
      version: v28.3.0
      release: traefik
      namespace: traefik
      repo:
        name: traefik
        url: "https://traefik.github.io/charts"
      values:
        image:
          registry: ghcr.io
          repository: traefik/traefik
        ingressClass:
          enabled: true
          isDefaultClass: false
        ingressRoute:
          dashboard:
            enabled: false
        ports:
          web:
            exposedPort: 80
          websecure:
            exposedPort: 443
        service:
          type: NodePort
        providers:
          kubernetesIngress:
            enabled: true
          kubernetesCRD:
            enabled: true
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 3m
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/traefik-ingressroute-crd.yaml
      namespace: sample
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    image.repository: "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx"
    image.tag: "1.27-alpine"
    ingress.enabled: "false"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: traefik
    timeout: 3m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/traefik-ingressroute-crd.sh
tags: [nightly]
mechanisms: ['addon:traefik']
category: networking
integration: traefik
tier: live

scenario.yaml 1902 B · 72 ln

---
id: ingress-controllers-traefik-middleware-chain
name: "Traefik middleware chain"
description: "Installs Traefik, creates a Middleware CR that injects custom headers, references it from an IngressRoute, and verifies the middleware effect is observable."
labels: {customer: any, profile: ingress}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: traefik/traefik
      version: v28.3.0
      release: traefik
      namespace: traefik
      repo:
        name: traefik
        url: "https://traefik.github.io/charts"
      values:
        image:
          registry: ghcr.io
          repository: traefik/traefik
        ingressClass:
          enabled: true
          isDefaultClass: false
        ingressRoute:
          dashboard:
            enabled: false
        ports:
          web:
            exposedPort: 80
          websecure:
            exposedPort: 443
        service:
          type: NodePort
        providers:
          kubernetesIngress:
            enabled: true
          kubernetesCRD:
            enabled: true
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 3m
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/traefik-middleware-headers.yaml
      namespace: sample
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/traefik-middleware-ingressroute.yaml
      namespace: sample
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    image.repository: "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx"
    image.tag: "1.27-alpine"
    ingress.enabled: "false"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: traefik
    timeout: 3m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/traefik-middleware-chain.sh
tags: [nightly]
mechanisms: ['addon:traefik']
category: networking
integration: traefik
tier: live

---
id: ingress-controllers-traefik-tls-passthrough
name: "Traefik TLS passthrough"
description: "Installs Traefik, configures IngressRouteTCP with tls.passthrough=true, and verifies the backend's TLS certificate is served untouched through the proxy."
labels: {customer: any, profile: tls}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: traefik/traefik
      version: v28.3.0
      release: traefik
      namespace: traefik
      repo:
        name: traefik
        url: "https://traefik.github.io/charts"
      values:
        image:
          registry: ghcr.io
          repository: traefik/traefik
        ingressClass:
          enabled: true
          isDefaultClass: false
        ingressRoute:
          dashboard:
            enabled: false
        ports:
          web:
            exposedPort: 80
          websecure:
            exposedPort: 443
        service:
          type: NodePort
        providers:
          kubernetesIngress:
            enabled: true
          kubernetesCRD:
            enabled: true
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 3m
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/traefik-tls-passthrough-ingressroutetcp.yaml
      namespace: sample
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/manual-tls-basic-secret.yaml
      namespace: sample
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    image.repository: "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx"
    image.tag: "1.27-alpine"
    ingress.enabled: "false"
    tls.enabled: "true"
    tls.secretName: "manual-tls-basic"
    tls.servicePort: "443"
    tls.initContainerImage: "public.ecr.aws/docker/library/busybox:1.36"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: traefik
    timeout: 3m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/traefik-tls-passthrough.sh
tags: [nightly]
mechanisms: ['addon:traefik']
category: networking
integration: traefik
tier: live

labels-off Capability: no extra-label keys leak when unset (OFF) PASS
Description
Renders the product chart with NO extra-label overrides and asserts that the configured test-label keys (team, cost-center) are absent from every rendered object's metadata. Since the chart has no extraLabels/commonLabels knob and the default render never emits these keys, this scenario is EXPECTED to PASS — confirming no label leakage.
Cluster
kind
Mechanisms
capability:labels
Tags
capabilitycompliance
Labels
customer=enterprise profile=compliance
Artifacts
Scenario YAML
scenario.yaml 852 B · 23 ln
View full file 
---
id: labels-off
name: "Capability: no extra-label keys leak when unset (OFF)"
description: >-
  Renders the product chart with NO extra-label overrides and asserts that the configured test-label keys (team, cost-center) are absent from every rendered object's metadata. Since the chart has no extraLabels/commonLabels knob and the default render never emits these keys, this scenario is EXPECTED to PASS — confirming no label leakage.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    ingress.enabled: true
asserts:
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/labels-absent.sh
tags: [capability, compliance]
category: capability
capability: label-all-objects
tier: capability
mechanisms: ["capability:labels"]

---
id: labels-on
name: "Capability: extra labels stamped on every object (ON)"
description: >-
  Renders the product chart with a global extra-label knob set (extraLabels.team=platform, extraLabels.cost-center=42) and asserts every rendered object (all kinds, not just pod templates) carries the configured labels at .metadata.labels. The sample chart does NOT expose an extraLabels/commonLabels knob — this scenario is EXPECTED to FAIL (honest red gap) documenting that the chart lacks global label propagation.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0

  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    ingress.enabled: true
    extraLabels.team: platform
    extraLabels.cost-center: "42"
asserts:
  - type: labels-present
    namespace: sample
    source: rendered
    labels:
      team: platform
      cost-center: "42"

id: minimal
name: "Vanilla cluster — no preinstalled addons"
description: "Baseline: chart installs and pods come up on a stock kind cluster."
labels: {customer: none, profile: baseline}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
asserts:
  - {type: helm-status-deployed, release: sample, namespace: sample}
  - {type: pods-ready, namespace: sample, timeout: 3m}
tags: [pr-subset, nightly]
mechanisms: ['addon:none']
category: capability
capability: baseline-deploy
tier: capability

helm_values:
  {replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, service: {type: ClusterIP, port: 80}, tls: {enabled: false, secretName: "", servicePort: 443,
      # -- Filesystem path where TLS cert+key are mounted. Defaults to /etc/tls.
      mountPath: "",
      # -- Volume type for the TLS material. Supported: secret (default), persistentVolumeClaim, projected, csi.
      volumeType: "secret",
      # -- PVC claim name (required when volumeType is persistentVolumeClaim).
      pvcClaimName: "",
      # -- SecretProviderClass name (required when volumeType is csi).
      secretProviderClass: "",
      # -- Whether to run the wait-for-tls initContainer that polls for cert files. Disable for CSI volumes that are populated asynchronously.
      waitForCerts: true},
    # -- Scope component (API server). Creates a separate Deployment + Service on port 8080.
    scope: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, service: {port: 8080}},
    # -- Darkroom component (async processor). Creates a separate Deployment with optional PVC mount.
    darkroom: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, pvc: {enabled: false, claimName: "", mountPath: /data}},
    # -- Ingress resource for skywatcher Service.
    ingress: {enabled: false, className: "nginx", host: "", path: /, pathType: Prefix},

    gatewayRoute: {enabled: false, parentRef: {name: envoy, namespace: "", sectionName: ""}, hostname: ""},

    mesh: {inject: false},

    policy: {complianceLabels: {}}}

network-policy-off Capability: no NetworkPolicy when disabled (OFF) PASS
Description
Renders the product chart with networkPolicy.enabled=false (or unset) and asserts zero NetworkPolicy documents in the render. Since the chart has no NetworkPolicy template at all, no NetworkPolicy objects are ever emitted regardless of the networkPolicy.enabled value. This scenario is EXPECTED to PASS — confirming no NetworkPolicy leakage when the knob is off.

kind
Mechanisms

scenario.yaml 913 B · 25 ln
View full file 
---
id: network-policy-off
name: "Capability: no NetworkPolicy when disabled (OFF)"
description: >-
  Renders the product chart with networkPolicy.enabled=false (or unset) and asserts zero NetworkPolicy documents in the render. Since the chart has no NetworkPolicy template at all, no NetworkPolicy objects are ever emitted regardless of the networkPolicy.enabled value. This scenario is EXPECTED to PASS — confirming no NetworkPolicy leakage when the knob is off.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    networkPolicy.enabled: false
asserts:
  - type: network-policy
    namespace: sample
    source: rendered
    expect_present: false
tags: [capability, compliance]
category: capability
capability: network-policy
tier: capability
mechanisms: ["capability:network-policy"]

---
id: network-policy-on
name: "Capability: NetworkPolicy present when enabled (ON)"
description: >-
  Renders the product chart with networkPolicy.enabled=true and asserts a NetworkPolicy is rendered selecting the product pods. The sample chart does NOT include a networkpolicy.yaml template — setting networkPolicy.enabled=true has no effect because the chart lacks the template. This scenario is EXPECTED to FAIL (honest red gap) documenting that the chart lacks a networkPolicy knob and template.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    networkPolicy.enabled: true
asserts:
  - type: network-policy
    namespace: sample
    source: rendered
    expect_present: true
tags: [capability, compliance]
category: capability
capability: network-policy
tier: capability
mechanisms: ["capability:network-policy"]

scenario.yaml 1924 B · 67 ln

---
id: networking-kong-ingress
name: "Kong Ingress (className=kong)"
description: >-
  Installs Kong Ingress Controller, deploys the product chart with ingress.enabled=true and ingress.className=kong, and verifies end-to-end routing through the Kong proxy data path via the chart's built-in Ingress resource. Also includes a KongPlugin gap-probe documenting that the sample chart exposes no konghq.com/plugins annotation or KongPlugin CRD knob, which is an honest gap (red cell) — do NOT over-engineer the chart.
labels: {customer: any, profile: ingress}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: kong/ingress
      version: 0.24.0
      release: kong
      namespace: kong
      repo:
        name: kong
        url: "https://charts.konghq.com"
      values:
        ingressController:
          enabled: true
          ingressClass: kong
          installCRDs: true
        proxy:
          type: NodePort
          http:
            enabled: true
            nodePort: 30080
          tls:
            enabled: true
            nodePort: 30443
        env:
          database: "off"
        replicaCount: 1
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "256Mi"
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 5m
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    image.repository: "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx"
    image.tag: "1.27-alpine"
    ingress.enabled: "true"
    ingress.className: "kong"
    ingress.host: "sample.test.local"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: kong
    timeout: 5m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/kong-ingress.sh
tags: [nightly, curated-live]
mechanisms: ['addon:kong']
category: networking
integration: kong
tier: live

scenario.yaml 1686 B · 60 ln

---
id: networking-metallb-loadbalancer
name: "MetalLB LoadBalancer (service.type=LoadBalancer)"
description: >-
  Installs MetalLB, configures an IPAddressPool + L2Advertisement whose CIDR is inside the kind Docker bridge subnet, deploys the product chart with service.type=LoadBalancer, and verifies that MetalLB assigns an external IP from the pool and the LB endpoint serves HTTP 200.
labels: {customer: any, profile: loadbalancer}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: metallb/metallb
      version: 0.16.1
      release: metallb
      namespace: metallb
      repo:
        name: metallb
        url: "https://metallb.github.io/metallb"
      values:
        controller:
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "50m"
              memory: "64Mi"
        speaker:
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "50m"
              memory: "64Mi"
        installCRDs: true
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 3m
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/metallb-ip-pool.yaml
      namespace: metallb
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    image.repository: "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx"
    image.tag: "1.27-alpine"
    service.type: "LoadBalancer"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: metallb
    timeout: 5m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/metallb-loadbalancer.sh
tags: [nightly, curated-live]
mechanisms: ['addon:metallb']
category: networking
integration: metallb
tier: live

scenario.yaml 1809 B · 69 ln
View full file 
---
id: networking-traefik-ingress
name: "Traefik Ingress (className=traefik)"
description: >-
  Installs Traefik, deploys the product chart with ingress.enabled=true and ingress.className=traefik, and verifies end-to-end routing through the Traefik data path via the chart's built-in Ingress resource.
labels: {customer: any, profile: ingress}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: traefik/traefik
      version: v28.3.0
      release: traefik
      namespace: traefik
      repo:
        name: traefik
        url: "https://traefik.github.io/charts"
      values:
        image:
          registry: ghcr.io
          repository: traefik/traefik
        ingressClass:
          enabled: true
          isDefaultClass: false
        ingressRoute:
          dashboard:
            enabled: false
        ports:
          web:
            exposedPort: 80
          websecure:
            exposedPort: 443
        service:
          type: NodePort
        providers:
          kubernetesIngress:
            enabled: true
          kubernetesCRD:
            enabled: true
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 3m
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    image.repository: "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx"
    image.tag: "1.27-alpine"
    ingress.enabled: "true"
    ingress.className: "traefik"
    ingress.host: "sample.test.local"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: traefik
    timeout: 3m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/traefik-ingress.sh
tags: [nightly, curated-live]
mechanisms: ['addon:traefik']
category: networking
integration: traefik
tier: live

scenario.yaml 1670 B · 60 ln

---
id: policy-kyverno-generate
name: "Kyverno generate: ConfigMap in labeled namespaces"
description: >-
  Installs Kyverno, creates a ClusterPolicy that generates a ConfigMap in any namespace labeled kyverno.io/generate=true. Verifies that creating a fresh namespace with the trigger label causes Kyverno to generate the ConfigMap within 10s. Webhook failure mode: Fail.
labels: {customer: any, profile: policy}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: kyverno/kyverno
      version: "3.8.1"
      release: kyverno
      namespace: kyverno
      repo:
        name: kyverno
        url: "https://kyverno.github.io/kyverno/"
      values:
        admissionController:
          replicas: 1
        backgroundController:
          enabled: true
        cleanupController:
          enabled: true
        reportsController:
          enabled: true
        features:
          admissionReports:
            enabled: true
          policyReports:
            enabled: true
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 4m
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/kyverno-generate-configmap.yaml
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    image.repository: "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx"
    image.tag: "1.27-alpine"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: kyverno
    timeout: 4m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/kyverno-generate.sh
tags: [nightly]
mechanisms: ['addon:kyverno']
category: policy
integration: kyverno
tier: live

---
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: generate-configmap-on-ns
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  background: true
  rules:
    - name: generate-default-configmap
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds:
                - Namespace
              selector:
                matchLabels:
                  kyverno.io/generate: "true"
      generate:
        synchronize: true
        apiVersion: v1
        kind: ConfigMap
        name: kyverno-generated-config
        namespace: "{{request.object.metadata.name}}"
        data:
          data:
            generated-by: "kyverno"
            namespace: "{{request.object.metadata.name}}"

scenario.yaml 1691 B · 60 ln

---
id: policy-kyverno-image-verify
name: "Kyverno image-verify: only approved registries"
description: >-
  Installs Kyverno, creates a ClusterPolicy that only allows images from public.ecr.aws/* or nginx* registries. Verifies a Pod referencing docker.io/library/redis:7-alpine is denied (stderr names rule), while a Pod with an approved image is accepted. Webhook failure mode: Fail.
labels: {customer: any, profile: policy}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: kyverno/kyverno
      version: "3.8.1"
      release: kyverno
      namespace: kyverno
      repo:
        name: kyverno
        url: "https://kyverno.github.io/kyverno/"
      values:
        admissionController:
          replicas: 1
        backgroundController:
          enabled: true
        cleanupController:
          enabled: true
        reportsController:
          enabled: true
        features:
          admissionReports:
            enabled: true
          policyReports:
            enabled: true
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 4m
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/kyverno-image-verify-allowlist.yaml
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    image.repository: "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx"
    image.tag: "1.27-alpine"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: kyverno
    timeout: 4m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/kyverno-image-verify.sh
tags: [nightly]
mechanisms: ['addon:kyverno']
category: policy
integration: kyverno
tier: live

---
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: image-registry-allowlist
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  background: true
  rules:
    - name: only-allowed-registries
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds:
                - Pod
      validate:
        message: "Images must come from approved registries (public.ecr.aws/* or nginx*)"
        anyPattern:
          - spec:
              containers:
                - image: "public.ecr.aws/*"
          - spec:
              containers:
                - image: "nginx*"

scenario.yaml 1642 B · 60 ln
View full file 
---
id: policy-kyverno-mutate
name: "Kyverno mutate: auto-add annotation to Pods"
description: >-
  Installs Kyverno, creates a ClusterPolicy that adds the annotation kyverno.io/managed-by: chart-test-swarm to Pods. Verifies a Pod manifest lacking the annotation gets it auto-added after the mutating webhook fires. Webhook failure mode: Fail.
labels: {customer: any, profile: policy}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: kyverno/kyverno
      version: "3.8.1"
      release: kyverno
      namespace: kyverno
      repo:
        name: kyverno
        url: "https://kyverno.github.io/kyverno/"
      values:
        admissionController:
          replicas: 1
        backgroundController:
          enabled: true
        cleanupController:
          enabled: true
        reportsController:
          enabled: true
        features:
          admissionReports:
            enabled: true
          policyReports:
            enabled: true
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 4m
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/kyverno-mutate-add-annotation.yaml
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    image.repository: "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx"
    image.tag: "1.27-alpine"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: kyverno
    timeout: 4m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/kyverno-mutate.sh
tags: [nightly]
mechanisms: ['addon:kyverno']
category: policy
integration: kyverno
tier: live

apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: add-managed-by-annotation
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  background: false
  rules:
    - name: add-managed-by
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds:
                - Pod
      mutate:
        patchesJson6902: |-
          - op: add
            path: /metadata/annotations/kyverno.io~1managed-by
            value: "chart-test-swarm"

---
id: policy-kyverno-validate
name: "Kyverno validate: require labels on Deployments"
description: >-
  Installs Kyverno, creates a ClusterPolicy that requires app.kubernetes.io/name label on Deployments. Verifies non-compliant Deployment denied (stderr names validate.kyverno.svc-fail and policy name), compliant Deployment accepted. Webhook failure mode: Fail.
labels: {customer: any, profile: policy}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: kyverno/kyverno
      version: "3.8.1"
      release: kyverno
      namespace: kyverno
      repo:
        name: kyverno
        url: "https://kyverno.github.io/kyverno/"
      values:
        admissionController:
          replicas: 1
        backgroundController:
          enabled: true
        cleanupController:
          enabled: true
        reportsController:
          enabled: true
        features:
          admissionReports:
            enabled: true
          policyReports:
            enabled: true
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 4m
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/kyverno-validate-require-label.yaml
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    image.repository: "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx"
    image.tag: "1.27-alpine"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: kyverno
    timeout: 4m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/kyverno-validate.sh
tags: [nightly]
mechanisms: ['addon:kyverno']
category: policy
integration: kyverno
tier: live

---
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-app-label
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  background: true
  rules:
    - name: require-app-kubernetes-io-name
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds:
                - Deployment
      validate:
        message: "Deployments must have the 'app.kubernetes.io/name' label"
        pattern:
          metadata:
            labels:
              app.kubernetes.io/name: "?*"

scenario.yaml 1570 B · 54 ln

---
id: policy-opa-gatekeeper-image-allowlist
name: "OPA Gatekeeper image allowlist enforcement"
description: >-
  Installs OPA Gatekeeper, creates k8sallowedrepos ConstraintTemplate + Constraint allowing only nginx + public.ecr.aws images. Verifies non-allowlisted image denied, allowlisted image accepted.
labels: {customer: any, profile: policy}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: gatekeeper/gatekeeper
      version: "3.17.1"
      release: gatekeeper
      namespace: gatekeeper-system
      repo:
        name: gatekeeper
        url: "https://open-policy-agent.github.io/gatekeeper/charts"
      values:
        auditInterval: 10
        constraintViolationsLimit: 20
        enableExternalData: false
        postInstall:
          labelNamespace:
            enabled: false
        validatingWebhookFailurePolicy: Fail
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 4m
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/k8sallowedrepos-template.yaml
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    image.repository: "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx"
    image.tag: "1.27-alpine"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: gatekeeper-system
    timeout: 4m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/opa-gatekeeper-image-allowlist.sh
tags: [nightly]
mechanisms: ['addon:opa-gatekeeper']
category: policy
integration: opa-gatekeeper
tier: live

---
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sallowedrepos
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sAllowedRepos
      validation:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            repos:
              type: array
              items:
                type: string
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8sallowedrepos
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          container := input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers[_]
          satisfied := [good | repo := input.parameters.repos[_]; good := startswith(container.image, repo)]
          not any(satisfied)
          msg := sprintf("Container '%v' uses disallowed registry: '%v'", [container.name, container.image])
        }

---
id: policy-opa-gatekeeper-required-labels
name: "OPA Gatekeeper required labels enforcement (gap-probe)"
description: >-
  Installs OPA Gatekeeper + NGINX Ingress, creates k8srequiredlabels ConstraintTemplate + Constraint targeting Deployments and Ingresses. Verifies non-compliant resources denied, compliant accepted. Cross-feature compose with M4 nginx-ingress. Then runs a gap-probe: the chart's Ingress template uses selectorLabels (just app: <release>) instead of the full common labels (which include app.kubernetes.io/name), so the chart's Ingress fails the required-labels constraint — an honest gap (red cell); do NOT over-engineer the chart.
labels: {customer: any, profile: policy}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: gatekeeper/gatekeeper
      version: "3.17.1"
      release: gatekeeper
      namespace: gatekeeper-system
      repo:
        name: gatekeeper
        url: "https://open-policy-agent.github.io/gatekeeper/charts"
      values:
        auditInterval: 10
        constraintViolationsLimit: 20
        enableExternalData: false
        postInstall:
          labelNamespace:
            enabled: false
        validatingWebhookFailurePolicy: Fail
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 4m
    - kind: helm
      chart: ingress-nginx/ingress-nginx
      version: "4.10.0"
      release: ingress-nginx
      namespace: ingress-nginx
      repo:
        name: ingress-nginx
        url: "https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx"
      values:
        controller:
          service:
            type: NodePort
          allowSnippetAnnotations: true
          ingressClassResource:
            name: nginx
            enabled: true
            default: false
            controllerValue: "k8s.io/ingress-nginx"
          watchIngressWithoutClass: true
        admissionWebhooks:
          enabled: false
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 3m
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/k8srequiredlabels-template.yaml
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    image.repository: "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx"
    image.tag: "1.27-alpine"
    ingress.enabled: "false"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: gatekeeper-system
    timeout: 4m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: ingress-nginx
    timeout: 3m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/opa-gatekeeper-required-labels.sh
tags: [nightly, curated-live]
mechanisms: ['addon:opa-gatekeeper', 'addon:nginx-ingress']
category: policy
integration: opa-gatekeeper
tier: live

---
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8srequiredlabels
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sRequiredLabels
      validation:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            labels:
              type: array
              items:
                type: string
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8srequiredlabels
        violation[{"msg": msg, "details": {"missing_labels": missing}}] {
          provided := {label | input.review.object.metadata.labels[label]}
          required := {label | label := input.parameters.labels[_]}
          missing := required - provided
          count(missing) > 0
          msg := sprintf("Missing required label(s): %v", [missing])
        }

---
id: policy-opa-gatekeeper-resource-limits
name: "OPA Gatekeeper resource limits enforcement"
description: >-
  Installs OPA Gatekeeper, creates k8scontainerlimits ConstraintTemplate + Constraint requiring CPU and memory limits on all containers. Verifies Deployment without limits denied, compliant Deployment accepted.
labels: {customer: any, profile: policy}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: gatekeeper/gatekeeper
      version: "3.17.1"
      release: gatekeeper
      namespace: gatekeeper-system
      repo:
        name: gatekeeper
        url: "https://open-policy-agent.github.io/gatekeeper/charts"
      values:
        auditInterval: 10
        constraintViolationsLimit: 20
        enableExternalData: false
        postInstall:
          labelNamespace:
            enabled: false
        validatingWebhookFailurePolicy: Fail
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 4m
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/k8scontainerlimits-template.yaml
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    image.repository: "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx"
    image.tag: "1.27-alpine"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: gatekeeper-system
    timeout: 4m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/opa-gatekeeper-resource-limits.sh
tags: [nightly]
mechanisms: ['addon:opa-gatekeeper']
category: policy
integration: opa-gatekeeper
tier: live

k8scontainerlimits-template.yaml 836 B · 27 ln

---
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8scontainerlimits
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sContainerLimits
      validation:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8scontainerlimits
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          container := input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers[_]
          not container.resources.limits.cpu
          msg := sprintf("Container '%v' missing cpu limit", [container.name])
        }
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          container := input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers[_]
          not container.resources.limits.memory
          msg := sprintf("Container '%v' missing memory limit", [container.name])
        }

scenario.yaml 1511 B · 53 ln

---
id: policy-opa-gatekeeper-sync-config
name: "OPA Gatekeeper sync configuration"
description: >-
  Installs OPA Gatekeeper, applies Gatekeeper Config with sync.syncOnly listing Namespace, Pod, and Ingress kinds for OPA cache sync. Verifies Config exists with non-empty syncOnly, controller Ready.
labels: {customer: any, profile: policy}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: gatekeeper/gatekeeper
      version: "3.17.1"
      release: gatekeeper
      namespace: gatekeeper-system
      repo:
        name: gatekeeper
        url: "https://open-policy-agent.github.io/gatekeeper/charts"
      values:
        auditInterval: 10
        constraintViolationsLimit: 20
        enableExternalData: false
        postInstall:
          labelNamespace:
            enabled: false
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 4m
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/gatekeeper-sync-config.yaml
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    image.repository: "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx"
    image.tag: "1.27-alpine"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: gatekeeper-system
    timeout: 4m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/opa-gatekeeper-sync-config.sh
tags: [nightly]
mechanisms: ['addon:opa-gatekeeper']
category: policy
integration: opa-gatekeeper
tier: live

description: >-
  Renders the product chart with default values (no priorityClassName override) and asserts that no workload pod spec carries a priorityClassName field. Since the chart has no priorityClassName template and no value is set, none should appear. This scenario is EXPECTED to PASS — confirming no priorityClassName leakage when unset.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
asserts:
  - type: priority-class-present
    namespace: sample
    source: rendered
    expect_present: false
tags: [capability, compliance]
category: capability
capability: priority-class-name
tier: capability
mechanisms: ["capability:priority"]

      mountPath: "",
      # -- Volume type for the TLS material. Supported: secret (default), persistentVolumeClaim, projected, csi.
      volumeType: "secret",
      # -- PVC claim name (required when volumeType is persistentVolumeClaim).
      pvcClaimName: "",
      # -- SecretProviderClass name (required when volumeType is csi).
      secretProviderClass: "",
      # -- Whether to run the wait-for-tls initContainer that polls for cert files. Disable for CSI volumes that are populated asynchronously.
      waitForCerts: true},
    # -- Scope component (API server). Creates a separate Deployment + Service on port 8080.
    scope: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, service: {port: 8080}},
    # -- Darkroom component (async processor). Creates a separate Deployment with optional PVC mount.
    darkroom: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, pvc: {enabled: false, claimName: "", mountPath: /data}},
    # -- Ingress resource for skywatcher Service.

    gatewayRoute: {enabled: false, parentRef: {name: envoy, namespace: "", sectionName: ""}, hostname: ""},
    # -- Service mesh integration.
    mesh: {inject: false},

    policy: {complianceLabels: {}}}

---
id: priority-class-on
name: "Capability: priorityClassName settable on ALL workloads (ON)"
description: >-
  Renders the product chart with priorityClassName=high-priority configured and asserts that every workload pod spec carries the priorityClassName with the configured value. The sample chart does NOT expose a priorityClassName knob in its values.yaml and has no priorityClassName field in any Deployment template — setting priorityClassName has no effect. This scenario is EXPECTED to FAIL (honest red gap) documenting that the chart lacks the priorityClassName scheduling knob.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    priorityClassName: high-priority
asserts:
  - type: priority-class-present
    namespace: sample
    source: rendered
    expect_present: true
    priority_class_name: high-priority
tags: [capability, compliance]
category: capability
capability: priority-class-name
tier: capability
mechanisms: ["capability:priority"]

rbac-off Capability: no RBAC objects when disabled (OFF) PASS
Description
Renders the product chart with rbac.create=false and asserts zero RBAC-kind objects (ServiceAccount, Role, ClusterRole, RoleBinding, ClusterRoleBinding) in the render. Since the chart has no RBAC templates at all, no RBAC objects are ever emitted regardless of the rbac.create value. This scenario is EXPECTED to PASS — confirming no RBAC objects leak when the knob is off.
Cluster
kind
Mechanisms
capability:rbac
Tags
capabilitycompliance
Labels
customer=enterprise profile=compliance
Artifacts
Scenario YAML
scenario.yaml 888 B · 25 ln
View full file 
---
id: rbac-off
name: "Capability: no RBAC objects when disabled (OFF)"
description: >-
  Renders the product chart with rbac.create=false and asserts zero RBAC-kind objects (ServiceAccount, Role, ClusterRole, RoleBinding, ClusterRoleBinding) in the render. Since the chart has no RBAC templates at all, no RBAC objects are ever emitted regardless of the rbac.create value. This scenario is EXPECTED to PASS — confirming no RBAC objects leak when the knob is off.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    rbac.create: false
asserts:
  - type: rbac-objects
    namespace: sample
    source: rendered
    expect_present: false
tags: [capability, compliance]
category: capability
capability: rbac-toggle
tier: capability
mechanisms: ["capability:rbac"]

resources-off Capability: no populated resources block when unset (OFF) PASS
Description
Renders the product chart with default values (no resources overrides) and asserts that no workload container carries a populated resources block. Since the skywatcher template has no resources block at all, and scope/darkroom are disabled, no populated resources block should appear. This scenario is EXPECTED to PASS — confirming no resources leakage when the knob is off.

kind

scenario.yaml 888 B · 23 ln

---
id: resources-off
name: "Capability: no populated resources block when unset (OFF)"
description: >-
  Renders the product chart with default values (no resources overrides) and asserts that no workload container carries a populated resources block. Since the skywatcher template has no resources block at all, and scope/darkroom are disabled, no populated resources block should appear. This scenario is EXPECTED to PASS — confirming no resources leakage when the knob is off.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
asserts:
  - type: resources-present
    namespace: sample
    source: rendered
    expect_present: false
tags: [capability, compliance]
category: capability
capability: resource-limits
tier: capability
mechanisms: ["capability:resources"]

      mountPath: "",

      volumeType: "secret",

resources-on Capability: resource requests/limits set on ALL workloads (ON) FAIL
Description
Renders the product chart with resources.requests and resources.limits configured (cpu=100m memory=128Mi / cpu=500m memory=256Mi) and asserts that every workload container carries the configured resources block. The scope and darkroom templates wire {{- with .Values.resources }} but the skywatcher Deployment does NOT include a resources block — setting resources has no effect on skywatcher. Scope and darkroom are not enabled in this scenario due to a pre-existing chart bug (scope readiness probe mismatch), but the skywatcher gap alone makes this scenario EXPECTED to FAIL (honest red gap). Scope and darkroom WOULD honor resources if enabled.

---
id: resources-on
name: "Capability: resource requests/limits set on ALL workloads (ON)"
description: >-
  Renders the product chart with resources.requests and resources.limits configured (cpu=100m memory=128Mi / cpu=500m memory=256Mi) and asserts that every workload container carries the configured resources block. The scope and darkroom templates wire {{- with .Values.resources }} but the skywatcher Deployment does NOT include a resources block — setting resources has no effect on skywatcher. Scope and darkroom are not enabled in this scenario due to a pre-existing chart bug (scope readiness probe mismatch), but the skywatcher gap alone makes this scenario EXPECTED to FAIL (honest red gap). Scope and darkroom WOULD honor resources if enabled.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    resources.requests.cpu: 100m
    resources.requests.memory: 128Mi
    resources.limits.cpu: 500m
    resources.limits.memory: 256Mi
asserts:
  - type: resources-present
    namespace: sample
    source: rendered
    expect_present: true
    requests:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
    limits:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 256Mi
tags: [capability, compliance]
category: capability
capability: resource-limits
tier: capability
mechanisms: ["capability:resources"]

      mountPath: "",

      volumeType: "secret",

      pvcClaimName: "",

      secretProviderClass: "",

      waitForCerts: true},
    # -- Scope component (API server). Creates a separate Deployment + Service on port 8080.
    scope: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, service: {port: 8080}},

---
id: scheduling-affinity-on
name: "Capability: affinity settable on ALL workloads (ON)"
description: >-
  Renders the product chart with a nodeAffinity rule configured (requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution preferring kubernetes.io/os=linux) and asserts that every workload pod spec carries the affinity block. The sample chart does NOT expose an affinity knob in its values.yaml and has no affinity block in any Deployment template — setting affinity has no effect. This scenario is EXPECTED to FAIL (honest red gap) documenting that the chart lacks the affinity scheduling knob.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    affinity.nodeAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.nodeSelectorTerms[0].matchExpressions[0].key: kubernetes.io/os
    affinity.nodeAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.nodeSelectorTerms[0].matchExpressions[0].operator: In
    affinity.nodeAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.nodeSelectorTerms[0].matchExpressions[0].values[0]: linux
asserts:
  - type: scheduling-present
    namespace: sample
    source: rendered
    expect_present: true
    check_nodeSelector: false
    check_tolerations: false
    check_affinity: true
    check_topologySpreadConstraints: false
    affinity:
      nodeAffinity: true
tags: [capability, compliance]
category: capability
capability: affinity
tier: capability
mechanisms: ["capability:scheduling"]

This scenario is EXPECTED to FAIL (honest red gap) documenting that the chart lacks the nodeSelector scheduling knob on its workloads.

---
id: scheduling-nodeselector-on
name: "Capability: nodeSelector settable on ALL workloads (ON)"
description: >-
  Renders the product chart with nodeSelector.disktype=ssd configured and asserts that every workload pod spec carries nodeSelector with the configured value. The sample chart does NOT expose a nodeSelector knob in its values.yaml and has no nodeSelector block in any Deployment template — setting nodeSelector has no effect. This scenario is EXPECTED to FAIL (honest red gap) documenting that the chart lacks the nodeSelector scheduling knob on its workloads.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    nodeSelector.disktype: ssd
asserts:
  - type: scheduling-present
    namespace: sample
    source: rendered
    expect_present: true
    check_nodeSelector: true
    check_tolerations: false
    check_affinity: false
    check_topologySpreadConstraints: false
    nodeSelector:
      disktype: ssd
tags: [capability, compliance]
category: capability
capability: node-selector
tier: capability
mechanisms: ["capability:scheduling"]

---
id: scheduling-off
name: "Capability: no scheduling fields when unset (OFF)"
description: >-
  Renders the product chart with default values (no nodeSelector, tolerations, affinity, or topologySpreadConstraints overrides) and asserts that no workload pod spec carries any of these scheduling fields. Since the chart has no scheduling templates and no values are set, none should appear. This scenario is EXPECTED to PASS — confirming no scheduling fields leak onto pod specs when unset.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
asserts:
  - type: scheduling-present
    namespace: sample
    source: rendered
    expect_present: false
    check_nodeSelector: true
    check_tolerations: true
    check_affinity: true
    check_topologySpreadConstraints: true
tags: [capability, compliance]
category: capability
capability: scheduling-off
tier: capability
mechanisms: ["capability:scheduling"]

---
id: scheduling-tolerations-on
name: "Capability: tolerations settable on ALL workloads (ON)"
description: >-
  Renders the product chart with a toleration configured (key=dedicated, operator=Equal, value=gpu, effect=NoSchedule) and asserts that every workload pod spec carries the toleration. The sample chart does NOT expose a tolerations knob in its values.yaml and has no tolerations block in any Deployment template — setting tolerations has no effect. This scenario is EXPECTED to FAIL (honest red gap) documenting that the chart lacks the tolerations scheduling knob.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    tolerations[0].key: dedicated
    tolerations[0].operator: Equal
    tolerations[0].value: gpu
    tolerations[0].effect: NoSchedule
asserts:
  - type: scheduling-present
    namespace: sample
    source: rendered
    expect_present: true
    check_nodeSelector: false
    check_tolerations: true
    check_affinity: false
    check_topologySpreadConstraints: false
    tolerations:
      - key: dedicated
        operator: Equal
        value: gpu
        effect: NoSchedule
tags: [capability, compliance]
category: capability
capability: tolerations
tier: capability
mechanisms: ["capability:scheduling"]

---
id: scheduling-topology-spread-on
name: "Capability: topologySpreadConstraints settable on ALL workloads (ON)"
description: >-
  Renders the product chart with a topologySpreadConstraint configured (maxSkew=1, topologyKey=topology.kubernetes.io/zone, whenUnsatisfiable=DoNotSchedule) and asserts that every workload pod spec carries the constraint. The sample chart does NOT expose a topologySpreadConstraints knob in its values.yaml and has no topologySpreadConstraints block in any Deployment template — setting the constraint has no effect. This scenario is EXPECTED to FAIL (honest red gap) documenting that the chart lacks the topologySpreadConstraints scheduling knob.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    topologySpreadConstraints[0].maxSkew: 1
    topologySpreadConstraints[0].topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
    topologySpreadConstraints[0].whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
    topologySpreadConstraints[0].labelSelector.matchLabels.app: sample
asserts:
  - type: scheduling-present
    namespace: sample
    source: rendered
    expect_present: true
    check_nodeSelector: false
    check_tolerations: false
    check_affinity: false
    check_topologySpreadConstraints: true
    topologySpreadConstraints:
      - topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
        maxSkew: 1
        whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
tags: [capability, compliance]
category: capability
capability: topology-spread-constraints
tier: capability
mechanisms: ["capability:scheduling"]

---
id: scheme-allow-http
name: "Capability: HTTP baseline scheme (OFF)"
description: >-
  Renders the product chart with default values (no TLS override) and asserts the plain-HTTP port 80 IS present on the Service, confirming the off-case baseline that the HTTPS-only knob must be able to suppress. This scenario is EXPECTED to PASS — the default render exposes port 80 (name: http) on the skywatcher Service.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    ingress.enabled: true
    ingress.host: sample.local
asserts:
  - type: scheme-enforced
    namespace: sample
    source: rendered
    scheme: allow-http
tags: [capability, compliance]
category: capability
capability: protocol-scheme
tier: capability
mechanisms: ["capability:scheme"]

helm_values:
  {replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, service: {type: ClusterIP, port: 80}, tls: {enabled: false, secretName: "", servicePort: 443,
      # -- Filesystem path where TLS cert+key are mounted. Defaults to /etc/tls.
      mountPath: "",
      # -- Volume type for the TLS material. Supported: secret (default), persistentVolumeClaim, projected, csi.
      volumeType: "secret",
      # -- PVC claim name (required when volumeType is persistentVolumeClaim).
      pvcClaimName: "",
      # -- SecretProviderClass name (required when volumeType is csi).
      secretProviderClass: "",
      # -- Whether to run the wait-for-tls initContainer that polls for cert files. Disable for CSI volumes that are populated asynchronously.
      waitForCerts: true},
    # -- Scope component (API server). Creates a separate Deployment + Service on port 8080.
    scope: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, service: {port: 8080}},
    # -- Darkroom component (async processor). Creates a separate Deployment with optional PVC mount.
    darkroom: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, pvc: {enabled: false, claimName: "", mountPath: /data}},
    # -- Ingress resource for skywatcher Service.
    ingress: {enabled: false, className: "nginx", host: "", path: /, pathType: Prefix},
    # -- HTTPRoute resource for Gateway API integration.
    gatewayRoute: {enabled: false, parentRef: {name: envoy, namespace: "", sectionName: ""}, hostname: ""},
    # -- Service mesh integration.
    mesh: {inject: false},
    # -- Policy compliance labels applied to pod templates.
    policy: {complianceLabels: {}}, ingress.enabled: true, ingress.host: sample.local}

scheme-https-only Capability: HTTPS-only scheme enforcement (ON) FAIL
Description
Renders the product chart with TLS enabled (tls.enabled=true) and asserts no plain-HTTP Service port, container port, probe, or Ingress backend is present. The sample chart does NOT support suppressing the HTTP port — when TLS is enabled it merely ADDS an HTTPS port (443) alongside the always-present HTTP port 80 on the Service, containerPort 80 on the Deployment, probes targeting port 80, and the Ingress backend pointing at service.port (80). This scenario is EXPECTED to FAIL (honest red gap) documenting that the chart lacks an HTTPS-only / http-disable knob. A TLS secret fixture is preinstalled so the chart can deploy with tls.enabled=true.

---
id: scheme-https-only
name: "Capability: HTTPS-only scheme enforcement (ON)"
description: >-
  Renders the product chart with TLS enabled (tls.enabled=true) and asserts no plain-HTTP Service port, container port, probe, or Ingress backend is present. The sample chart does NOT support suppressing the HTTP port — when TLS is enabled it merely ADDS an HTTPS port (443) alongside the always-present HTTP port 80 on the Service, containerPort 80 on the Deployment, probes targeting port 80, and the Ingress backend pointing at service.port (80). This scenario is EXPECTED to FAIL (honest red gap) documenting that the chart lacks an HTTPS-only / http-disable knob. A TLS secret fixture is preinstalled so the chart can deploy with tls.enabled=true.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/manual-tls-basic-secret.yaml
      namespace: sample
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    tls.enabled: true
    tls.secretName: manual-tls-basic
    ingress.enabled: true
    ingress.host: sample.local
asserts:
  - type: scheme-enforced
    namespace: sample
    source: rendered
    scheme: https-only
tags: [capability, compliance, curated-live]
category: capability
capability: protocol-scheme
tier: capability
mechanisms: ["capability:scheme"]

      mountPath: "",

      volumeType: "secret",
      # -- PVC claim name (required when volumeType is persistentVolumeClaim).
      pvcClaimName: "",

      secretProviderClass: "",

      waitForCerts: true},

    scope: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, service: {port: 8080}},

- apiVersion: v1
  data:
    default.conf: |
      server {
        listen 80;
        server_name _;
        location / {
          root /usr/share/nginx/html;
          index index.html;
        }
      }
      server {
        listen 443 ssl;
        server_name _;
        ssl_certificate     /etc/tls/tls.crt;
        ssl_certificate_key /etc/tls/tls.key;
        location / {
          root /usr/share/nginx/html;
          index index.html;
        }
      }

security-context-off Capability: no securityContext when knobs unset (OFF) PASS
Description
Renders the product chart with default values (no securityContext overrides) and asserts that no pod-level or container-level securityContext block is present on any workload. Since the chart has no securityContext templates, no securityContext blocks are ever emitted. This scenario is EXPECTED to PASS — confirming no securityContext leakage when the knob is off.

---
id: security-context-off
name: "Capability: no securityContext when knobs unset (OFF)"
description: >-
  Renders the product chart with default values (no securityContext overrides) and asserts that no pod-level or container-level securityContext block is present on any workload. Since the chart has no securityContext templates, no securityContext blocks are ever emitted. This scenario is EXPECTED to PASS — confirming no securityContext leakage when the knob is off.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
asserts:
  - type: security-context
    namespace: sample
    source: rendered
    expect_present: false
tags: [capability, compliance]
category: capability
capability: pod-security
tier: capability
mechanisms: ["capability:security-context"]

      mountPath: "",

---
id: security-context-on
name: "Capability: pod/container securityContext knobs set (ON)"
description: >-
  Renders the product chart with pod-security and container-security knobs set (podSecurityContext.runAsNonRoot=true, podSecurityContext.seccompProfile.type=RuntimeDefault, securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem=true, securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation=false, securityContext.capabilities.drop[0]=ALL) and asserts pod-level and container-level securityContext fields appear with the configured values. The sample chart does NOT expose podSecurityContext or securityContext values and has no securityContext blocks in its templates — setting these knobs has no effect. This scenario is EXPECTED to FAIL (honest red gap) documenting that the chart lacks securityContext knobs.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    podSecurityContext.runAsNonRoot: true
    podSecurityContext.seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault
    securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
    securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
    securityContext.capabilities.drop[0]: ALL
asserts:
  - type: security-context
    namespace: sample
    source: rendered
    expect_present: true
    podSecurityContext:
      runAsNonRoot: true
      seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault
    containerSecurityContext:
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
      capabilities.drop: ALL
tags: [capability, compliance]
category: capability
capability: pod-security
tier: capability
mechanisms: ["capability:security-context"]

service-mesh-istio-ambient-live Istio Ambient Mesh — Live mTLS Verification (ztunnel/HBONE) PASS
Description
Installs istio/base + istio/istiod (profile=ambient) + istio/cni (profile=ambient) + istio/ztunnel, annotates the product namespace istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambient via raw_manifest, deploys the chart with mesh.inject=false (NO sidecar), and proves: (1) ztunnel DaemonSet pods are Ready in istio-system, (2) the product namespace carries the ambient annotation and every product pod has exactly 1 container (no istio-proxy), (3) in-mesh traffic to the product Service returns HTTP 200 and the connection is mTLS over HBONE — confirmed via ztunnel metrics/logs. Emits a PASS artifact bundle with 1-container pod manifest, ambient-annotated namespace manifest, applied-overrides recording inject: false, and versions.json.
Cluster
kind
Preinstalled
istio-base, istiod, istio-cni, ztunnel

---
id: service-mesh-istio-ambient-live
name: "Istio Ambient Mesh — Live mTLS Verification (ztunnel/HBONE)"
description: >-
  Installs istio/base + istio/istiod (profile=ambient) + istio/cni (profile=ambient) + istio/ztunnel, annotates the product namespace istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambient via raw_manifest, deploys the chart with mesh.inject=false (NO sidecar), and proves: (1) ztunnel DaemonSet pods are Ready in istio-system, (2) the product namespace carries the ambient annotation and every product pod has exactly 1 container (no istio-proxy), (3) in-mesh traffic to the product Service returns HTTP 200 and the connection is mTLS over HBONE — confirmed via ztunnel metrics/logs. Emits a PASS artifact bundle with 1-container pod manifest, ambient-annotated namespace manifest, applied-overrides recording inject: false, and versions.json.
labels: {customer: any, profile: mesh}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/base
      version: 1.27.9
      release: istio-base
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values: {}
      wait: helm-deployed
      wait_timeout: 2m
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/istiod
      version: 1.27.9
      release: istiod
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values:
        profile: ambient
        pilot:
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "384Mi"
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 5m
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/cni
      version: 1.27.9
      release: istio-cni
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values:
        profile: ambient
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 3m
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/ztunnel
      version: 1.27.9
      release: ztunnel
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values: {}
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 3m
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/istio-ambient-namespace.yaml
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    mesh.inject: "false"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: istio-base
    namespace: istio-system
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: istiod
    namespace: istio-system
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: istio-cni
    namespace: istio-system
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: ztunnel
    namespace: istio-system
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: istio-system
    selector: app=ztunnel
    timeout: 5m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: istio-system
    selector: app=istiod
    timeout: 5m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/istio-ambient-live.sh
tags: [nightly, curated-live]
mechanisms: ['addon:istio-ambient', 'mesh:istio-ambient']
category: service-mesh
integration: istio-ambient
tier: live

helm_values:
  {replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, service: {type: ClusterIP, port: 80}, tls: {enabled: false, secretName: "", servicePort: 443,
      # -- Filesystem path where TLS cert+key are mounted. Defaults to /etc/tls.
      mountPath: "",
      # -- Volume type for the TLS material. Supported: secret (default), persistentVolumeClaim, projected, csi.
      volumeType: "secret",
      # -- PVC claim name (required when volumeType is persistentVolumeClaim).
      pvcClaimName: "",
      # -- SecretProviderClass name (required when volumeType is csi).
      secretProviderClass: "",
      # -- Whether to run the wait-for-tls initContainer that polls for cert files. Disable for CSI volumes that are populated asynchronously.
      waitForCerts: true},
    # -- Scope component (API server). Creates a separate Deployment + Service on port 8080.
    scope: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, service: {port: 8080}},
    # -- Darkroom component (async processor). Creates a separate Deployment with optional PVC mount.
    darkroom: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, pvc: {enabled: false, claimName: "", mountPath: /data}},
    # -- Ingress resource for skywatcher Service.
    ingress: {enabled: false, className: "nginx", host: "", path: /, pathType: Prefix},
    # -- HTTPRoute resource for Gateway API integration.
    gatewayRoute: {enabled: false, parentRef: {name: envoy, namespace: "", sectionName: ""}, hostname: ""},
    # -- Service mesh integration.
    mesh: {inject: false},
    # -- Policy compliance labels applied to pod templates.
    policy: {complianceLabels: {}}, mesh.inject: "false"}

---
id: service-mesh-istio-ingress-gateway-basic
name: "Istio Ingress Gateway — Basic"
description: >-
  Installs istio/base + istio/istiod + istio/gateway, deploys the product chart with ingress disabled, creates an Istio Gateway + VirtualService to route external traffic through the ingressgateway pod, and verifies HTTP 200 via the gateway with a Host header.
labels: {customer: any, profile: mesh}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/base
      version: 1.27.9
      release: istio-base
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values: {}
      wait: helm-deployed
      wait_timeout: 2m
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/istiod
      version: 1.27.9
      release: istiod
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values:
        pilot:
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "384Mi"
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 5m
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/gateway
      version: 1.27.9
      release: istio-ingressgateway
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values:
        service:
          type: NodePort
          ports:
            - name: http2
              port: 80
              nodePort: 30080
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 3m
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    ingress.enabled: false
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: istio-base
    namespace: istio-system
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: istiod
    namespace: istio-system
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: istio-ingressgateway
    namespace: istio-system
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: istio-system
    selector: app=istiod
    timeout: 5m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: istio-system
    selector: app=istio-ingressgateway
    timeout: 3m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 3m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/istio-ingress-gateway-basic.sh
tags: [nightly, curated-live]
mechanisms: ['addon:istio', 'mesh:istio-ingress-gateway']
category: service-mesh
integration: istio
tier: live

scenario.yaml 2607 B · 91 ln

---
id: service-mesh-istio-ingress-gateway-jwt
name: "Istio Ingress Gateway — JWT Authentication"
description: >-
  Installs istio/base + istio/istiod + istio/gateway, deploys the product chart, creates an Istio Gateway + VirtualService, applies a RequestAuthentication + AuthorizationPolicy requiring a valid JWT, and verifies: (a) requests without a Bearer token are rejected with 401/403, (b) requests with a valid JWT signed by the test issuer key from fixtures/service-mesh/jwt/ return HTTP 200.
labels: {customer: any, profile: mesh}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/base
      version: 1.27.9
      release: istio-base
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values: {}
      wait: helm-deployed
      wait_timeout: 2m
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/istiod
      version: 1.27.9
      release: istiod
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values:
        pilot:
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "384Mi"
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 5m
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/gateway
      version: 1.27.9
      release: istio-ingressgateway
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values:
        service:
          type: NodePort
          ports:
            - name: http2
              port: 80
              nodePort: 30080
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 3m
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    ingress.enabled: false
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: istio-base
    namespace: istio-system
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: istiod
    namespace: istio-system
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: istio-ingressgateway
    namespace: istio-system
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: istio-system
    selector: app=istiod
    timeout: 5m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: istio-system
    selector: app=istio-ingressgateway
    timeout: 3m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 3m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/istio-ingress-gateway-jwt.sh
tags: [nightly]
mechanisms: ['addon:istio', 'mesh:istio-ingress-gateway']
category: service-mesh
integration: istio
tier: live
