---
id: service-mesh-istio-ingress-gateway-multi-host
name: "Istio Ingress Gateway — Multi-Host"
description: >-
  Installs istio/base + istio/istiod + istio/gateway, deploys the product chart with scope.enabled=true, creates an Istio Gateway with two server blocks for different hosts, and a VirtualService that routes each host to a different backend (skywatcher vs scope). Verifies both hosts return HTTP 200 through the ingressgateway.
labels: {customer: any, profile: mesh}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/base
      version: 1.27.9
      release: istio-base
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values: {}
      wait: helm-deployed
      wait_timeout: 2m
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/istiod
      version: 1.27.9
      release: istiod
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values:
        pilot:
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "384Mi"
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 5m
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/gateway
      version: 1.27.9
      release: istio-ingressgateway
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values:
        service:
          type: NodePort
          ports:
            - name: http2
              port: 80
              nodePort: 30080
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 3m
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    ingress.enabled: false
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: istio-base
    namespace: istio-system
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: istiod
    namespace: istio-system
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: istio-ingressgateway
    namespace: istio-system
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: istio-system
    selector: app=istiod
    timeout: 5m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: istio-system
    selector: app=istio-ingressgateway
    timeout: 3m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 3m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/istio-ingress-gateway-multi-host.sh

mechanisms: ['addon:istio', 'mesh:istio-ingress-gateway']

---
id: service-mesh-linkerd-live
name: "Linkerd — Live mTLS Sidecar Mesh"
description: >-
  Installs linkerd-crds + linkerd-control-plane (with a preinstalled trust anchor / issuer cert via raw_manifest), annotates the product namespace with linkerd.io/inject=enabled, deploys the chart, and proves: (1) linkerd control-plane pods Ready and proxy-injector webhook present, (2) every product pod has a linkerd-proxy container alongside the app container, (3) linkerd check --proxy -n sample exits 0 confirming the data plane is healthy. Emits a PASS artifact bundle with a 2-container pod manifest, linkerd.io/inject-annotated namespace, and versions.json.
labels: {customer: any, profile: mesh}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    # Step 1: Install Linkerd CRDs (required before control-plane)
    - kind: helm
      chart: linkerd/linkerd-crds
      version: 1.8.0
      release: linkerd-crds
      namespace: linkerd
      repo:
        name: linkerd
        url: "https://helm.linkerd.io/stable"
      values: {}
      wait: helm-deployed
      wait_timeout: 2m
    # Step 2: Pre-create linkerd namespace + identity issuer Secret (trust anchor via raw_manifest)
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/linkerd-identity-secret.yaml
    # Step 3: Install Linkerd control plane with REPLACE_AT_RUNTIME cert placeholders.
    # linkerd-live.sh generates real ephemeral certs and upgrades the release before
    # any other checks run, so the initial install uses wait:none (pods won't be Ready
    # with placeholder certs).
    - kind: helm
      chart: linkerd/linkerd-control-plane
      version: 1.16.11
      release: linkerd-control-plane
      namespace: linkerd
      repo:
        name: linkerd
        url: "https://helm.linkerd.io/stable"
      values: ./fixtures/linkerd-live-values.yaml
      wait: none
    # Step 4: Annotate the product namespace for linkerd injection (before product chart install)
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/linkerd-inject-namespace.yaml
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set: {}
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: linkerd-crds
    namespace: linkerd
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: linkerd-control-plane
    namespace: linkerd
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/linkerd-live.sh
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: linkerd
    timeout: 10m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
tags: [nightly, curated-live]
mechanisms: ['addon:linkerd', 'mesh:linkerd']
category: service-mesh
integration: linkerd
tier: live

# Linkerd control-plane values for chart-test-swarm kind clusters.
# Certs and keys are generated at runtime by the linkerd-gen-certs.sh assertion script.
# REPLACE_AT_RUNTIME markers are substituted with ephemeral ECDSA P-256 certs.
# DO NOT add real private key material to this file.
proxy:
  resources:
    cpu:
      limit: "250m"
      request: "100m"
    memory:
      limit: "256Mi"
      request: "64Mi"
identity:
  issuer:
    scheme: linkerd.io/tls
    tls:
      crtPEM: REPLACE_AT_RUNTIME
      keyPEM: REPLACE_AT_RUNTIME
identityTrustAnchorsPEM: REPLACE_AT_RUNTIME

serviceaccount-annotations-off Capability: ServiceAccount identity annotations absent when unset (OFF) PASS
Description
Renders the product chart with serviceAccount.create=true and no annotation overrides, then asserts the ServiceAccount does NOT carry any cloud-identity annotation keys (IRSA, Azure WI, GKE WI). The sample chart does NOT include a serviceaccount.yaml template — no ServiceAccount is rendered at all. Since no ServiceAccount exists, the off-case is vacuously satisfied. This scenario is EXPECTED to PASS — confirming no cloud-identity annotation leakage (and no ServiceAccount) when the knob is off.
Cluster
kind
Mechanisms
capability:serviceaccount-annotations
Tags
capabilitycompliance
Labels
customer=enterprise profile=compliance

---
id: serviceaccount-annotations-off
name: "Capability: ServiceAccount identity annotations absent when unset (OFF)"
description: >-
  Renders the product chart with serviceAccount.create=true and no annotation overrides, then asserts the ServiceAccount does NOT carry any cloud-identity annotation keys (IRSA, Azure WI, GKE WI). The sample chart does NOT include a serviceaccount.yaml template — no ServiceAccount is rendered at all. Since no ServiceAccount exists, the off-case is vacuously satisfied. This scenario is EXPECTED to PASS — confirming no cloud-identity annotation leakage (and no ServiceAccount) when the knob is off.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    serviceAccount.create: true
asserts:
  - type: serviceaccount-annotations
    namespace: sample
    source: rendered
    expect_present: false
    identity_keys:
      - eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn
      - azure.workload.identity/client-id
      - iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account
tags: [capability, compliance]
category: capability
capability: serviceaccount-identity
tier: capability
mechanisms: ["capability:serviceaccount-annotations"]

scenario.yaml 1363 B · 28 ln
View full file 
---
id: serviceaccount-annotations-on
name: "Capability: ServiceAccount cloud-identity annotations settable (ON)"
description: >-
  Renders the product chart with serviceAccount.annotations configured for AWS IRSA (eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn) and asserts the rendered ServiceAccount carries the exact annotation key/value. The sample chart does NOT include a serviceaccount.yaml template — no ServiceAccount is rendered. Setting serviceAccount.annotations has no effect because the chart lacks both a ServiceAccount template and a serviceAccount.annotations knob. This scenario is EXPECTED to FAIL (honest red gap) documenting that the chart lacks ServiceAccount cloud-identity annotation support.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    serviceAccount.create: true
    serviceAccount.annotations.eks\\.amazonaws\\.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/demo
asserts:
  - type: serviceaccount-annotations
    namespace: sample
    source: rendered
    expect_present: true
    annotations:
      eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/demo
tags: [capability, compliance]
category: capability
capability: serviceaccount-identity
tier: capability
mechanisms: ["capability:serviceaccount-annotations"]

---
id: tls-cert-manager-self-signed
name: "cert-manager self-signed Issuer -> CA Cert -> CA Issuer -> leaf Cert"
description: >-
  Installs cert-manager with CRDs, applies a self-signed Issuer, a CA Certificate bootstrapping a CA Secret, a CA Issuer backed by that Secret, and a leaf Certificate for the product Service FQDN. Deploys chart with tls.enabled=true and tls.secretName pointing at the issued Secret. Verifies HTTPS 200 with --cacert and SAN match.
labels: {customer: any, profile: tls}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: jetstack/cert-manager
      version: v1.14.0
      release: cert-manager
      namespace: cert-manager
      repo:
        name: jetstack
        url: "https://charts.jetstack.io"

# Leaf Certificate — signed by the CA Issuer.
# The product chart consumes the resulting TLS Secret.
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: sample-tls
  namespace: sample
spec:
  secretName: sample-tls
  duration: 24h
  renewBefore: 12h
  issuerRef:
    name: chart-test-swarm-ca-issuer
    kind: Issuer
  commonName: "sample.sample.svc"
  dnsNames:
    - "sample.sample.svc"
    - "sample.sample.svc.cluster.local"

metadata:
  name: chart-test-swarm-selfsigned-issuer
  namespace: sample
spec:
  selfSigned: {}

---
id: tls-manual-secret
name: "Manual TLS Secret via raw_manifest"
description: >-
  Delivers a pre-provisioned kubernetes.io/tls Secret (RSA 2048) via raw_manifest preinstall sourced from chart-test/fixtures/, no inline base64 blobs. The chart mounts it with tls.volumeType=secret (default) and serves HTTPS 200. Validates Secret type, data keys, PEM validity, and in-cluster HTTPS reachability.
labels: {customer: any, profile: tls}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/manual-tls-basic-secret.yaml
      namespace: sample
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    tls.enabled: "true"
    tls.secretName: manual-tls-basic
    tls.servicePort: "443"
    tls.volumeType: "secret"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/manual-tls-basic.sh
tags: [nightly, curated-live]
mechanisms: ['addon:manual-tls-secret']
category: certificates
integration: manual-tls-secret
tier: live

  {replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, service: {type: ClusterIP, port: 80}, tls: {enabled: false, secretName: "", servicePort: 443,
      # -- Filesystem path where TLS cert+key are mounted. Defaults to /etc/tls.
      mountPath: "",
      # -- Volume type for the TLS material. Supported: secret (default), persistentVolumeClaim, projected, csi.
      volumeType: "secret",
      # -- PVC claim name (required when volumeType is persistentVolumeClaim).
      pvcClaimName: "",
      # -- SecretProviderClass name (required when volumeType is csi).
      secretProviderClass: "",
      # -- Whether to run the wait-for-tls initContainer that polls for cert files. Disable for CSI volumes that are populated asynchronously.
      waitForCerts: true},
    # -- Scope component (API server). Creates a separate Deployment + Service on port 8080.
    scope: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, service: {port: 8080}},
    # -- Darkroom component (async processor). Creates a separate Deployment with optional PVC mount.
    darkroom: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, pvc: {enabled: false, claimName: "", mountPath: /data}},
    # -- Ingress resource for skywatcher Service.
    ingress: {enabled: false, className: "nginx", host: "", path: /, pathType: Prefix},
    # -- HTTPRoute resource for Gateway API integration.
    gatewayRoute: {enabled: false, parentRef: {name: envoy, namespace: "", sectionName: ""}, hostname: ""},
    # -- Service mesh integration.
    mesh: {inject: false},
    # -- Policy compliance labels applied to pod templates.
    policy: {complianceLabels: {}}, tls.enabled: "true", tls.secretName: manual-tls-basic, tls.servicePort: "443", tls.volumeType: "secret"}

      kubernetes.io/description: Contains a CA bundle that can be used to verify the
        kube-apiserver when using internal endpoints such as the internal service
        IP or kubernetes.default.svc. No other usage is guaranteed across distributions
        of Kubernetes clusters.

- apiVersion: v1
  data:
    default.conf: |
      server {
        listen 80;
        server_name _;
        location / {
          root /usr/share/nginx/html;
          index index.html;
        }
      }
      server {
        listen 443 ssl;
        server_name _;
        ssl_certificate     /etc/tls/tls.crt;
        ssl_certificate_key /etc/tls/tls.key;
        location / {
          root /usr/share/nginx/html;
          index index.html;
        }
      }

Description
Creates a kubernetes.io/tls Secret, then deploys the chart with tls.volumeType=projected so the pod has a projected volume sourcing the TLS Secret. Verifies projected volume source, tls.crt/tls.key present at mountPath, and in-cluster HTTPS curl returns 200.

---
id: tls-mounted-projected
name: "TLS via projected volume"
description: >-
  Creates a kubernetes.io/tls Secret, then deploys the chart with tls.volumeType=projected so the pod has a projected volume sourcing the TLS Secret. Verifies projected volume source, tls.crt/tls.key present at mountPath, and in-cluster HTTPS curl returns 200.
labels: {customer: any, profile: tls}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/mounted-tls-projected-secret.yaml
      namespace: sample
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    tls.enabled: "true"
    tls.secretName: mounted-tls-projected
    tls.servicePort: "443"
    tls.volumeType: "projected"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/mounted-tls-projected-volume.sh
tags: [nightly, curated-live]
mechanisms: ['addon:mounted-tls-certs']
category: certificates
integration: mounted-tls-certs
tier: live

  {replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, service: {type: ClusterIP, port: 80}, tls: {enabled: false, secretName: "", servicePort: 443,
      # -- Filesystem path where TLS cert+key are mounted. Defaults to /etc/tls.
      mountPath: "",
      # -- Volume type for the TLS material. Supported: secret (default), persistentVolumeClaim, projected, csi.
      volumeType: "secret",
      # -- PVC claim name (required when volumeType is persistentVolumeClaim).
      pvcClaimName: "",
      # -- SecretProviderClass name (required when volumeType is csi).
      secretProviderClass: "",
      # -- Whether to run the wait-for-tls initContainer that polls for cert files. Disable for CSI volumes that are populated asynchronously.
      waitForCerts: true},
    # -- Scope component (API server). Creates a separate Deployment + Service on port 8080.
    scope: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, service: {port: 8080}},
    # -- Darkroom component (async processor). Creates a separate Deployment with optional PVC mount.
    darkroom: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, pvc: {enabled: false, claimName: "", mountPath: /data}},
    # -- Ingress resource for skywatcher Service.
    ingress: {enabled: false, className: "nginx", host: "", path: /, pathType: Prefix},
    # -- HTTPRoute resource for Gateway API integration.
    gatewayRoute: {enabled: false, parentRef: {name: envoy, namespace: "", sectionName: ""}, hostname: ""},
    # -- Service mesh integration.
    mesh: {inject: false},
    # -- Policy compliance labels applied to pod templates.
    policy: {complianceLabels: {}}, tls.enabled: "true", tls.secretName: mounted-tls-projected, tls.servicePort: "443", tls.volumeType: "projected"}

  data:
    default.conf: |
      server {
        listen 80;
        server_name _;
        location / {
          root /usr/share/nginx/html;
          index index.html;
        }
      }
      server {
        listen 443 ssl;
        server_name _;
        ssl_certificate     /etc/tls/tls.crt;
        ssl_certificate_key /etc/tls/tls.key;
        location / {
          root /usr/share/nginx/html;
          index index.html;
        }
      }

---
id: tls-mounted-pvc
name: "TLS via persistentVolumeClaim"
description: >-
  Creates a PVC, populates it with TLS certs via a Job, then deploys the chart with tls.volumeType=persistentVolumeClaim and tls.pvcClaimName pointing at the pre-populated PVC. Verifies the pod mount, cert files at mountPath, and in-cluster HTTPS curl returns 200. Artifact bundle records the exact volumeType=persistentVolumeClaim.
labels: {customer: any, profile: tls}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/mounted-tls-pvc.yaml
      namespace: sample
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/mounted-tls-pvc-certs-configmap.yaml
      namespace: sample
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/mounted-tls-populate-job.yaml
      namespace: sample
product:
  chart: ./chart

---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: populate-mounted-tls-pvc
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
        - name: populate
          image: busybox:1.36
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              base64 -d /certs-in/tls.crt.b64 > /certs-out/tls.crt
              base64 -d /certs-in/tls.key.b64 > /certs-out/tls.key
              chmod 644 /certs-out/tls.crt /certs-out/tls.key
              echo "TLS certs written to PVC"
              ls -la /certs-out/
              [ -f /certs-out/tls.crt ] && [ -s /certs-out/tls.crt ] && echo "tls.crt OK" || { echo "FAIL: tls.crt missing or empty"; exit 1; }
              [ -f /certs-out/tls.key ] && [ -s /certs-out/tls.key ] && echo "tls.key OK" || { echo "FAIL: tls.key missing or empty"; exit 1; }
          volumeMounts:
            - name: certs-in
              mountPath: /certs-in
            - name: certs-out
              mountPath: /certs-out
      volumes:
        - name: certs-in
          configMap:
            name: mounted-tls-pvc-certs
        - name: certs-out
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: mounted-tls-pvc

- apiVersion: v1
  data:
    default.conf: |
      server {
        listen 80;
        server_name _;
        location / {
          root /usr/share/nginx/html;
          index index.html;
        }
      }
      server {
        listen 443 ssl;
        server_name _;
        ssl_certificate     /etc/tls/tls.crt;
        ssl_certificate_key /etc/tls/tls.key;
        location / {
          root /usr/share/nginx/html;
          index index.html;
        }
      }

scenario.yaml 787 B · 27 ln

id: with-cert-manager
name: "Customer ships cert-manager preinstalled"
description: "Validates chart coexists with cert-manager and its CRDs."
labels: {customer: any, profile: tls}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - chart: jetstack/cert-manager
      version: v1.14.0
      release: cert-manager
      namespace: cert-manager
      repo: {name: jetstack, url: "https://charts.jetstack.io"}
      values: {installCRDs: true}
      wait: pods-ready
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
asserts:
  - {type: helm-status-deployed, release: sample, namespace: sample}
  - {type: pods-ready, namespace: sample}
tags: [pr-subset, nightly]
mechanisms: ['addon:cert-manager']
category: certificates
integration: cert-manager
tier: live

      # -- Filesystem path where TLS cert+key are mounted. Defaults to /etc/tls.
      mountPath: "",
      # -- Volume type for the TLS material. Supported: secret (default), persistentVolumeClaim, projected, csi.
      volumeType: "secret",
      # -- PVC claim name (required when volumeType is persistentVolumeClaim).
      pvcClaimName: "",
      # -- SecretProviderClass name (required when volumeType is csi).
      secretProviderClass: "",
      # -- Whether to run the wait-for-tls initContainer that polls for cert files. Disable for CSI volumes that are populated asynchronously.
      waitForCerts: true},
    # -- Scope component (API server). Creates a separate Deployment + Service on port 8080.
    scope: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, service: {port: 8080}},
    # -- Darkroom component (async processor). Creates a separate Deployment with optional PVC mount.
    darkroom: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, pvc: {enabled: false, claimName: "", mountPath: /data}},
    # -- Ingress resource for skywatcher Service.
    ingress: {enabled: false, className: "nginx", host: "", path: /, pathType: Prefix},
    # -- HTTPRoute resource for Gateway API integration.
    gatewayRoute: {enabled: false, parentRef: {name: envoy, namespace: "", sectionName: ""}, hostname: ""},
    # -- Service mesh integration.
    mesh: {inject: false},
    # -- Policy compliance labels applied to pod templates.
    policy: {complianceLabels: {}}}
